newsitem.title: DUBAI: Dubai gold sales for Diwali below expectations.
newsitem.headline: Dubai gold sales for Diwali below expectations.

text.p: Gold jewellery and bullion purchases in Dubai by Indian expatriates celebrating India's festival of Diwali (Light) have been up to 15 percent below last year's turnover, Dubai jewellery traders said on Sunday.

Sales in the main 22-carat jewellery mart have been depressed by the Gulf state's new residency laws which has led to more than 167,000 workers -- mainly from the Indian subcontinent -- leaving under a three-month amnesty, traders said.
"Compared to last year it is not as good...people are more hesitant to spend money now because of the amnesty," a leading jeweller said on the Gulf state's tighter labour laws.

The United Arab Emirates has clamped down on thousands of expatriate workers without proper work and residency papers, saying the size of the illegal labour market in the state comprised of seven emirates posed a security threat.
Though most of the workers were on modest salaries and far from being major gold buyers, traders said that the expulsions had made people more conservative with their spending.
Business in Dubai this Diwali had also been affected by the Moslem week-end which clashed on Friday with India's Dhanteras, the day when gold and other gifts is bought for Diwali.

Some Indian shop owners in the Dubai souk, who estimated trade down by between five and 15 percent, said that many customers were unsure if shops would be open on a Friday when business is usually closed for the Moslem holiday.
Diwali, which was celebrated by Hindus on Sunday, and India's two main wedding seasons are the prime motors behind the Dubai precious metals market.
The festival of light traditionally sees Dubai's majority Indian expatriate community buying 21 and 22 carat jewellery mostly in the form of bangles, necklaces and earrings.
Bullion is also bought in small pieces of gold in sizes usually between five and 15 grammes.

In contrast to local sales, bullion re-exports to India from Dubai remained buoyant because of modest prices, an attractive trading arbitrage, Indian economic reform and the wedding season which starts in the coming weeks, traders said.
Dubai's benchmark Ten Tola (TT) bar -- 3.746 ounces of 24 carat gold -- was quoted by Dubai traders on Sunday at 5,245 UAE dirhams ($1,428.37), up from 5,225 dirhams.
Ten gram pieces were pegged at 448 dirhams, up one dirham.
International spot bullion was last quoted on Saturday at $379.35-75 an ounce, up from the London Friday fix of $378.15 but below the year-on-year comparison of $389. ($1=3.67 UAE dirhams)
